text:
noah: Short thread: we should add a runtime blacklist that prevents certain models from using the lowest-bitfallbacks during peak hours. Idea: peak_policy {start, end, banned_fallbacks}.
tara: Makes sense for latency-sensitive endpoints. How to toggle? Ops console + API.
ben: Also expose per-customer overrides, some enterprise customers pay for higher quality guarantees. Use tenant_profile to enforce stronger baselines.
alexa: For metrics, we need a per-tenant quality_violations counter that increments when degrade_score > threshold. That maps to billing hooks eventually.
ops-bot: Policy change: added peak_policy for endpoint /text/generate, banned_fallbacks=[4bit].
noah: Add note: runtime should reject policy if it conflicts with a customer's contract minimum_quality. We need a policy validator during apply.
tara: Also add audit log for policy changes with who/why/timestamp.
ben: For experiments, support a "soft-ban" where runtime prefers but may still use the fallback if capacity exhausted and a last-resort flag.
alexa: We'll need to record reason codes in responses: reason=capacity_pressure vs policy_block.
noah: Ok will file a tiny RFC patch with: peak_policy shape, tenant_profile mapping, audit log, soft-ban semantics, and response reason codes. Posting link soon.
